expectation.reason: The published decomposition contains one complete upper chord but only a bass note below it. Framework v0 must not promote that incomplete lower unit to a polychord layer.

The peer-reviewed transcription and analysis establish two complete, pitch-class-disjoint minor triads in separate registers and attacks; the possible integrated extension is substantially less concise.
The source-established two-triad construction supports a secondary polychord annotation, while the same pitch-class collection and exact bass support C9/G as the primary reading.

The literature supports the two-triad construction, but Framework v0 requires a distinct sounded note for each layer assignment and cannot reuse this A-flat/G-sharp. The product must therefore abstain on this exact snapshot.
The score establishes a two-unit construction, but the product symbol remains unresolved and the contiguous-register baseline cannot recover it.

The verified score's two separately transposed parallel major-triad streams support a secondary constructional reading, while the competing octatonic interpretation remains explicit in the research record.
The two triadic streams are source-attested, but this endpoint is exactly Gm7 and the analysis places both streams in one G-Dorian space; motion support alone must not force a secondary annotation.
The score and pedagogical analysis establish disjoint complete units with different roots, while the union has no concise conventional single-chord symbol.
Neither of two exact assignments for the same G|C identity should create a secondary annotation when the generated observation is explicitly one integrated Cmaj9 voicing.
A two-hand realization explicitly generated as one seventh chord must not acquire an Em|C annotation merely because its lower three and upper three notes each form a complete triad.
A conventional integrated major-thirteenth-sharp-eleventh name explains the complete collection, so the mechanical split must not authorize a secondary annotation.
The incomplete lower shell and conventional dominant extension keep this outside the initial positive scope.
The explicit generation recipe exercises the symmetric seventh-chord vocabulary on the upper layer.
An ordinary integrated sixth chord must not acquire a secondary polychord annotation solely because its doubled notes admit a split.
The explicit construction, register assignment, and separate onset cohorts support the secondary decomposition while preserving C9/G as the primary alternative for the exact voicing.
Register duplication of one chord must remain one chord.
The explicit two-triad construction and register boundary support the secondary annotation while retaining the integrated alternative.
